answer: We model a Sybil-resistant system employing dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and zero-knowledge verifiable delay, mandating staking collateral in a cryptographic vault prior to state mutations. A subgame-perfect slashing matrix across a juniper topology imposes slashing penalties upon detecting identity multiplication, irreversibly confiscating adversarial capital. Across this horizon, these cryptoeconomic primitives guarantee strictly negative expected utility for Sybil attacks, converging the multi-agent system into a robust Nash equilibrium.
